levels.label: Unclear
levels.description: Important goals, users, constraints, or assumptions are missing or contradictory.

levels.label: Partial
levels.description: Some goals and constraints are named, but key ambiguities remain unresolved.

levels.label: Coherent
levels.description: The main goals, constraints, assumptions, and open questions are stated clearly.

levels.label: Well bounded
levels.description: Priorities, measurable constraints, assumptions, and follow-up questions are separated and traceable.

levels.label: Unclear
levels.description: The proposed parts and their responsibilities or interactions cannot be followed.

levels.label: Partial
levels.description: Some parts are identified, but important ownership or data-flow boundaries are absent.

levels.label: Coherent
levels.description: Major responsibilities, boundaries, and flows connect to the stated requirements.

levels.label: Traceable
levels.description: The design makes ownership and critical flows explicit and relates them to constraints.

levels.label: Unclear
levels.description: Choices are asserted without naming costs, constraints, or alternatives.

levels.label: Partial
levels.description: A benefit or cost is named, but the decision is weakly tied to the case constraints.

levels.label: Reasoned
levels.description: The main choice, its cost, and a relevant alternative are tied to stated constraints.

levels.label: Explicit
levels.description: The decision boundary, rejected alternative, consequences, and conditions for revisiting it are clear.

levels.label: Incomplete
levels.description: The response omits a stage or does not provide a usable conclusion.

levels.label: Partial
levels.description: All stages have a response, but the final summary leaves important decisions implicit.

levels.label: Complete
levels.description: The final response summarizes requirements, architecture, and key tradeoffs.

levels.label: Integrated
levels.description: The final response connects decisions to priorities, risks, and the next validation step.

cases.title: Reliable webhook delivery
cases.brief: Design a multi-tenant webhook delivery service. Customers register endpoints and subscribe to events. The service must deliver each event promptly, tolerate endpoint outages, avoid unbounded retry work, and let customers inspect delivery history. No throughput, retention, or delivery guarantee is specified; identify the assumptions you need before committing to a design.

reviewCriteria.description: Clarify delivery guarantees, latency expectations, tenant isolation, retention, and endpoint trust assumptions.
Explain event intake, durable delivery state, scheduling, workers, endpoint calls, and customer-visible status.
Discuss retries, duplicate delivery, backpressure, endpoint failure, and the cost of stronger guarantees.
Summarize the chosen flow, guarantees, major risks, and a useful validation step.

cases.title: Collaborative project workspace
cases.brief: Design the frontend architecture for a collaborative project workspace used on desktop and mobile browsers. Users browse large project lists, edit shared records, and may temporarily lose connectivity. Accessibility and responsive behavior are required. The product has no fixed framework or traffic profile; state your assumptions and keep the design framework-neutral.

reviewCriteria.description: Clarify user journeys, collaboration behavior, offline expectations, accessibility needs, and device constraints.
Explain route and view boundaries, state ownership, data flow, rendering, and server interaction.
Discuss consistency, performance, offline behavior, accessibility, and implementation complexity tradeoffs.
Summarize the user-visible flow, state strategy, key tradeoffs, and a useful validation step.

cases.title: Library loan lifecycle
cases.brief: Model the domain for a library loan service. A member may borrow eligible copies, return or renew a loan, and incur a hold when no copy is available. The system must preserve loan limits and prevent the same physical copy from being actively loaned twice. Describe behavior and ownership without assuming a particular language or persistence technology.

reviewCriteria.description: Clarify member eligibility, copy availability, renewal rules, holds, and the invariants that must always hold.
Assign state and behavior to domain concepts and explain the collaboration for borrow, return, and renewal.
Discuss invariant ownership, concurrency, extension points, and the cost of alternative responsibility boundaries.
Summarize the core model, protected invariants, major tradeoffs, and a useful validation step.
